item.name: HelpAddActionButtonText
item.heading: Text
item.description:
The button text. This is an actual name of your button which will be shown on the panel.
Example: "Restart server"

item.name: HelpAddActionButtonDescription
item.heading: Description
item.description:
An optional description. It is shown under the button name and as a tooltip when you point at the button.
Example: "This button restarts specified server"

item.name: HelpAddActionButtonScript
item.heading: Script
item.description:
The script file to run. How the path is read depends on "Path is".
If "Relative to the config folder": give the path from the folder that contains config.json. Both / and \ separators work on every system. Example: scripts/restart_server.ps1
If "Absolute": give the full path. Windows: C:\scripts\restart_server.ps1 macOS / Linux: /Users/you/scripts/restart_server.ps1
Use Browse to pick the file; EasyJob chooses the right path type and script type for you.

item.name: HelpAddActionButtonScriptPathType
item.heading: Script path type
item.description:
Relative: the script path starts from the folder that contains config.json (shown in the status bar). Absolute: the script can be anywhere on your computer and you give its full path.
Example: Relative to the config folder

item.name: HelpAddActionButtonScriptType
item.heading: Script type
item.description:
How the script is run:
PowerShell (.ps1): with pwsh, or Windows PowerShell on Windows. Python (.py): with python3. Shell (.sh): with /bin/bash or /bin/sh on macOS and Linux. Command prompt (.bat, .cmd): with cmd.exe on Windows. On macOS and Linux this type runs the file with /bin/sh.
Example: PowerShell

item.name: HelpAddActionButtonArguments
item.heading: Arguments
item.description:
Arguments the script needs. Each one is asked for before the script runs (with the prompt text you write), and what you type is passed to the script, in this order.
Example: "Please specify server DNS name or IP address"

item.name: HelpConfigurationDefaultPowershellPath
item.heading: Default PowerShell path
item.description:
Full path to the PowerShell executable. Leave empty to use pwsh (or powershell on Windows) found on your PATH. Set it to pick a specific version.
Examples: macOS / Linux: /usr/local/bin/pwsh Windows: C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe

item.name: HelpConfigurationDefaultCMDPath
item.heading: Default CMD path
item.description:
Windows only. Full path to the command prompt. Leave empty to use cmd.exe from the system.
Example: C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe

item.name: HelpConfigurationPowerShellArguments
item.heading: PowerShell arguments
item.description:
Additional parameters sent to PowerShell.
Example: -ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted

item.name: HelpConfigurationConsoleBackground
item.heading: Console background
item.description:
Background color of the output panels. Use a color name or a hex value.
Examples: Black, #0C0C0C

item.name: HelpConfigurationConsoleForeground
item.heading: Console foreground
item.description:
Default text color of the output panels. Use a color name or a hex value.
Examples: White, #E6E6E6

item.name: HelpConfigurationPowerShellNativeColors
item.heading: PowerShell's own colors
item.description:
Show the colors PowerShell itself produces: red errors, table headers, and Write-Host -ForegroundColor / -BackgroundColor. Turn it off to run scripts with plain -File and no color handling.
Example: Yes

item.name: HelpConfigurationOpenCommandsPanel
item.heading: Commands panel in the script editor
item.description:
Open the PowerShell commands panel automatically when the script editor opens. You can still show or hide it with the button in the editor or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P. Once you toggle it, editor windows opened later in the same session keep that choice.
Example: Yes

item.name: HelpConfigurationCheckUpdates
item.heading: Check for updates
item.description:
Look for a newer EasyJob release on GitHub each time the app starts. When there is one, an Update button appears in the menu bar. You can also use Help -> Check for updates at any time.
Example: Yes

item.name: HelpConfigurationConfigReadonly
item.heading: Read-only configuration
item.description:
Nothing can be changed or saved: tabs, buttons and settings stay exactly as they are in config.json. Theme and button size changes last only for the session. Combine it with a read-only config.json and a policy.json (see the README) for a fully managed setup.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationScriptEditorReadonly
item.heading: Script editor read-only
item.description:
The script editor opens scripts for reading and running only: no typing, saving or new files.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationConfirmBeforeRun
item.heading: Confirm before every run
item.description:
Ask "Run this script?" every time a script is started, from a button, the editor or Run again.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockScriptEditor
item.heading: Block the script editor
item.description:
Turns the script editor off completely: menus, Shift+click and "Edit in script editor" are gone, and the PowerShell command browser with it.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockScriptEditorRun
item.heading: Block running from the editor
item.description:
The editor can still show and edit scripts, but has no Run button and F5 does nothing.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockScriptEditorOpenFiles
item.heading: Block opening other files in the editor
item.description:
The editor only opens scripts from the script buttons (Shift+click / Edit in script editor). The Open buttons and File -> Open file are gone.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockPowershellCommands
item.heading: Block the PowerShell command browser
item.description:
Hides the Commands panel in the script editor and Tools -> PowerShell commands.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockEditorTerminal
item.heading: Block the terminal in the script editor
item.description:
Removes the Terminal tab under the script editor. The terminal is also unavailable while running scripts from the editor is blocked, while the allowed script types or folders are restricted, or while every run needs confirmation, because a terminal could bypass those rules.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockOpenScriptExternally
item.heading: Block Open with default app
item.description:
Removes "Open with default app" from the script menu.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockShowInFolder
item.heading: Block Show in folder
item.description:
Removes "Show in folder" and Ctrl/Cmd+click on a script button.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockUpdates
item.heading: Block updates
item.description:
EasyJob never checks GitHub for new versions and never updates itself. Use this when you roll out updates yourself.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockViewSettings
item.heading: Block theme and button size changes
item.description:
Removes Theme and Button size from the View menu and the size toggle in the tab strip.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideTools
item.heading: Hide the Tools menu
item.description:
Hides the whole Tools menu (Script editor, PowerShell commands and Configuration).
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideViewEventLog
item.heading: Hide the event log
item.description:
Hides the Events button in the footer and View → Show or hide event log.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationClearEventsWhenReload
item.heading: Clear events when reload
item.description:
Clear events on Events list after configuration reload from the File-> Reload config menu.
Example: Yes

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockTabsRemove
item.heading: Block removing tabs
item.description:
Users cannot remove tabs: Tabs → Remove current tab and the tab right-click menu entry are gone.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockButtonsRemove
item.heading: Block removing script buttons
item.description:
Users cannot remove script buttons: "Remove…" is gone from the script button menu.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockTabsAdd
item.heading: Block adding tabs
item.description:
Users cannot add tabs (New tab in the tab strip and the Tabs menu). This also stops reordering tabs.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockButtonsAdd
item.heading: Block adding script buttons
item.description:
Users cannot add script buttons: Add script (tab strip), Scripts → Add script button and the panel right-click entry are gone.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockButtonsReorder
item.heading: Block reordering script buttons
item.description:
Reorder in the tab strip, Scripts → Reorder script buttons and dragging buttons to reorder them are disabled.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockButtonsEdit
item.heading: Block editing script buttons
item.description:
"Edit…" is gone from the script button menu, so buttons cannot be changed.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockTabsRename
item.heading: Block renaming tabs
item.description:
Tabs → Rename current tab and the tab right-click entry are gone.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockButtonsPaste
item.heading: Block pasting script buttons
item.description:
Paste (tab strip, Scripts menu and the panel right-click menu) is gone.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationBlockButtonsCopy
item.heading: Block copying script buttons
item.description:
"Copy" is gone from the script button menu.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideFileReloadConfig
item.heading: Hide File → Reload config
item.description:
Hides File → Reload config (and its F5 shortcut).
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideFileOpenAppFolder
item.heading: Hide File → Open config folder
item.description:
Hides File → Open config folder.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideClearEventsList
item.heading: Hide View → Clear event log
item.description:
Hides View → Clear event log.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettings
item.heading: Hide the settings group (Tools → Configuration)
item.description:
Hides the settings entry of the Tools menu, which is Configuration. To bring it back you have to edit config.json by hand.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettingsWorkflow
item.heading: Hide the Tabs and Scripts menus
item.description:
Hides the Tabs menu and the Scripts menu. The tab strip buttons follow the individual settings below.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettingsWorkflowReorderTabs
item.heading: Hide Tabs → Reorder tabs
item.description:
Hides Tabs → Reorder tabs.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettingsWorkflowAddTab
item.heading: Hide Tabs → New tab
item.description:
Hides Tabs → New tab and the New tab button in the tab strip.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettingsWorkflowRemoveCurrentTab
item.heading: Hide Tabs → Remove current tab
item.description:
Hides Tabs → Remove current tab.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettingsWorkflowRenameCurrentTab
item.heading: Hide Tabs → Rename current tab
item.description:
Hides Tabs → Rename current tab.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettingsWorkflowAddButtonToCurrentTab
item.heading: Hide Scripts → Add script button
item.description:
Hides Scripts → Add script button and the Add script button in the tab strip.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettingsWorkflowReorderButtonsInCurrentTab
item.heading: Hide Scripts → Reorder script buttons
item.description:
Hides Scripts → Reorder script buttons and the Reorder button in the tab strip.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideSettingsConfiguration
item.heading: Hide Tools → Configuration
item.description:
Hides Tools → Configuration. To bring it back you have to edit config.json by hand.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideHelp
item.heading: Hide the Help menu
item.description:
Hides the whole Help menu.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideTroubleshooting
item.heading: Hide Help → Troubleshooting
item.description:
Hides Help → Troubleshooting.
Example: No

item.name: HelpConfigurationHideAbout
item.heading: Hide Help → About EasyJob
item.description:
Hides Help → About EasyJob.
Example: No
